name: SimPrune
backbones: DeiT-T; DeiT-S; DeiT-B (DINO); MoCo v3; DINOv2
main_result: DeiT-S (DINO, ImageNet-1k linear eval): 62.31 at 76% training FLOPs (DINO baseline 62.49 at 100%; EViT 60.06, ToMe 60.34) with keep rate 0.8
notes: [core] Token pruning for ViTs during self-supervised pre-training, with ImageNet results on DeiT-T/S/B against EViT and ToMe. The goal is cheaper SSL training, not faster inference: tokens are pruned only inside the two DINO branches during pre-training, and accuracy is linear-probe accuracy, so no supervised DeiT-S top-1 or inference GFLOPs is given (deits columns left ?). Each online-branch token is matched to its most similar target-branch token (cosine) and token pairs are pruned by similarity; a sliding window moves linearly over the epochs from pruning the most dissimilar pairs to pruning the most similar ones (difficulty-aware). Extra tokens in the target branch (many-to-one matches) are removed by attention-based pruning. Pruning at blocks 4, 7, 10 with a fixed keep rate (0.9/0.8/0.7). Encoders trained 300 epochs on ImageNet-1k from scratch (fine-grained sets start from ImageNet weights). Only relative training time is reported (A100), no inference latency. No code link in the paper. Also COCO detection and ADE20K segmentation after SSL pre-training.
evidence: "we introduce a similarity-based token pruning method that uses cross-branch similarity information to pair and prune tokens" (1. Introduction); "To address this issue, we propose using an attention-based pruning approach to further prune tokens in the target branch" (4.1); "we perform the token pruning at the 4th, 7th, and 10th transformer blocks of DeiT for all the evaluated approaches" (5.1); "The encoders are DeiT-T, DeiT-S, and DeiT-B, which are trained on ImageNet-1k for 300 epochs." (Table 3)

name: PRO-SCALE
backbones: Mask2Former with Swin-T; ResNet-50; MViTv2-T (also MaskDINO, open-vocabulary FC-CLIP style models)
main_result: Swin-T Mask2Former (COCO panoptic): PQ 52.82 at 171.7 GFLOPs, encoder 56.18 GFLOPs (M2F 52.03 at 234.5, encoder 117.0)
notes: [core] Token length reduction in the multi-scale transformer encoder of Mask2Former with a clear segmentation evaluation, but the backbone is a CNN or Swin and the tokens are encoder feature queries. The encoder has three stages: stage 1 sees only the smallest-scale tokens (s4), stage 2 adds s3, stage 3 adds s2, each repeated p1/p2/p3 times, so large-scale tokens skip the early encoder layers (operation other: tokens are added progressively, no token is scored). A light pixel embedding (max-pooling) replaces the convolutions on s1, and a token recalibration module enriches small-scale tokens. Same lengths for every image. The whole segmentation model is trained (COCO 50 epochs, Cityscapes 90k iterations) from ImageNet-pretrained backbones, as for Mask2Former; the encoder is not taken from a trained model (training scratch, as for Lite-DETR in g8). FPS on A6000 in the ablation table (Cityscapes); batch size not stated.
evidence: "The underlying principle of PRO-SCALE is: progressively scale the length of the tokens with the layers of the encoder." (Abstract); "gradually expanding the token length of inputs to intermediate layers in PRO-SCALE" (3.1); "For COCO, our models are trained for 50 epochs." (Appendix, training details)

name: DAR
main_result: DINOv2-B (DUTS salient object segmentation): F-beta-w 0.901 at 91.54 GFLOPs, 28.11 FPS (AdaptFormer without reduction 0.906 at 118.70 GFLOPs, 27.71 FPS; DyT 0.859 at 95.51 GFLOPs)
notes: [core] Token reduction combined with parameter-efficient fine-tuning of a frozen ViT for pixel-level tasks (salient, camouflaged, polyp, skin lesion segmentation, defocus blur). Name: Diverse Attention Restorer (DAR). In each block a 3x3 conv on the patch-token grid, a sigmoid with Gumbel noise in training and a threshold T=0.5 give a per-token mask; masked tokens skip the FFN but stay in the sequence (attention, class/register tokens and a convolutional token compensator still see the full grid), so the operation is closest to halt per block. The activation rate is steered to a target (0.3/0.5/0.7) by a rate loss, but the count varies per image through the threshold. Only the PEFT module, token compensator and mask generator are trained; FFN and other block modules stay frozen. FPS measured on an RTX 4060 Ti; batch size not stated. Name taken from the paper text.
evidence: "we introduce the idea of using a learnable mask as the token reduction strategy" (3.2); "Then, we apply a sigmoid function followed by a threshold operation to generate masks" (3.2); "During inference, we remove the Gumbel noise and apply Mi directly to Xi to determine which tokens to mask at FFN" (3.2); "During training, the PEFT module, token compensator, and token reduction components are tuned, while FFN and other modules within the transformer block remain fixed." (Fig. 2)

name: TCA
backbones: CLIP ViT-B/16; CLIP ViT-L/14; SigLIP ViT-B/16; SigLIP 2 ViT-B/16
main_result: CLIP ViT-B/16 (cross-dataset benchmark, 10 datasets): average top-1 68.69 at 15.45 GFLOPs with R=0.9 (CLIP 64.59 at 17.59; TDA 67.53; EViT 65.17 at 15.41; ToMe 64.88 at 15.31)
notes: [vlm?] Token condensation in the CLIP / SigLIP image encoder used as training-free test-time adaptation for zero-shot classification; reduction is a means for adaptation and also lowers GFLOPs. Tokens are ranked by class-token attention per head, using the current class token together with a domain anchor token (stored low-entropy class tokens of earlier test samples), and the averaged relative ranking across heads decides: the lowest tokens are pruned and a middle band of ambiguous tokens is merged into K=2 centres chosen by greedy k-centre coreset selection and averaging (operation cluster). A fixed fraction R of tokens is kept (R=0.9 or 0.7 in the main table). Logits are also corrected by the stored anchors. Batch size 1, A6000; only GFLOPs, no wall-clock time. No code link in the paper.
evidence: "Rather than passively discarding tokens, TCA condenses token representation by introducing reservoir-based domain anchor tokens for information-preserving token reduction and logits correction." (Abstract); "evaluates the token importance individually for each attention head with the consideration of saved domain anchor tokens" (3.4); "we propose a domain-aware token merging strategy to consolidate these tokens into more representative ones" (3.4); "Notably, our method is training-free, enabling rapid adaptation with minimal hyperparameter dependency." (4.1)

name: Representation Shift
backbones: DeiT-T; DeiT-S; DeiT-B; UMT-B; UMT-L; ResNet-34; ResNet-50; Vision Mamba (ViM-T)
main_result: DeiT-S (ImageNet-1k, with FlashAttention): top-1 77.8 at 3.0 GFLOPs, 5948 img/s (baseline 79.8 at 4.6, 3002 img/s; class-attention pruning 72.1 at 3.0, 4844 img/s)
notes: [core] Training-free token pruning score that works with FlashAttention because it needs no attention map; evaluated on DeiT ImageNet and on UMT video-text retrieval and video QA (up to 5.5x speedup). The score is the L2 distance between a token before and after the MLP, i.e. the magnitude of the MLP update (criterion norm in the sense of an update magnitude, not the token norm). DeiT: 20% of tokens pruned at layers 1, 4, 7; UMT: 20% (retrieval) or 10% (QA) in each of the first three layers. Throughput on RTX A6000, batch 512 for DeiT, batch 20 for UMT. The ViT and video results are training-free; the ResNet variant (row/column pruning) is fine-tuned for 100 epochs, hence mixed. Also used as the importance metric inside vid-TLDR and on ViM.
evidence: "We compute the L2 distance between token representations before and after the MLP layer to quantify how much each token is emphasized by the transformation." (Fig. 2); "After quantifying the importance of the tokens in the [1,4,7] layers of DeiT, we pruned the 20% tokens at each layer." (4.2); "For vision transformers, we use DeiT [52] without additional training" (4.2); "we finetune the model for 100 epochs, including 10 cooldown epochs to refine this change" (4.2, ResNet)

name: ToSA
backbones: SigLIP so400m-patch14-384 in SpatialBot-Phi2-3B and LLaVA-OneVision-7B
main_result: LLaVA-OV-7B (VQAv2 counting): relative counting accuracy 64.1 with 50% of visual tokens (ToMe 53.1; full 77.1); SigLIP encoder 23.7 img/s at 50% tokens (full 18.2, ToMe 23.8) on V100
notes: [vlm?] Training-free ToMe-style merging inside the SigLIP vision encoder of VLMs, evaluated only on spatial / counting / embodied QA (SpatialBench, VQAv2 counting, GQA, OpenEQA with 12 frames); published at IROS with a robotics motivation and needs a depth map (predicted by Depth Anything V2). Spatial tokens are built from the (x, y, depth level) of each patch with positional encoding; bipartite soft matching uses a fused score alpha*S_visual + (1-alpha)*S_spatial with alpha = i/L rising over the layers, and spatial tokens are merged along with visual tokens. Retain ratios 50% and 10% of tokens. Throughput of the vision encoder only, batch size not stated.
evidence: "We present ToSA, a training-free token merging method that conducted token merging based on semantic similarity and spatial awareness." (I. Introduction); "ToSA takes the visual tokens and spatial tokens as input, and calculates two separate score matrices" (III.C); "In the default setting, we use a linear increase schedule for α, which gradually increases when passing through the layers of ViT." (III.C)

name: LookWhere
main_result: ViT-S (ImageNet-1k): top-1 80.3 at 3.8 GFLOPs, 9.5K img/s with k=128 (DINOv2 ViT-S 81.9 at 6.2 GFLOPs, 6.8K img/s; DTEM 79.4 at 2.4, 7.0K) on RTX 4090
notes: [core] Token selection before the ViT with ImageNet and ADE20K results against token reduction methods (PiToMe, DTEM, ATC). A shallow low-resolution selector (3 layers, 154 px input) predicts a patch-importance map, and only the top-k high-resolution patches plus the selector's low-resolution global tokens enter the extractor, so unselected patches are never computed (operation prune at the input). Selector and extractor are pretrained jointly by distillation from DINOv2 (class token, patch tokens, and the teacher attention map for the selector), starting from DINOv2 weights; per task only the extractor and a head are fine-tuned (30 epochs on ImageNet), the selector stays frozen. k is fixed per setting. The model is a DINOv2 ViT-S, not DeiT-S, so the deits columns are left ?. Also high-resolution Traffic Signs, CUB and Billiards (up to 34x fewer FLOPs). Throughput batch size not stated in the main text.
evidence: "Only the top k most informative patches are selected from the high-resolution input." (2.1); "By distilling the teacher’s attention, the selector learns to predict the location of deep, salient information given only shallow, low-resolution input." (2.3); "Initialization. We set the selector and extractor parameters to those of the teacher: DINOv2." (2.3); "we only update the predictor-extractor without updating the selector or needing the teacher" (2.2)

name: CAIT
backbones: DeiT-T; DeiT-S; DeiT-B; LV-ViT; Swin-T; Swin-S
main_result: DeiT-S (ImageNet-1k): top-1 80.2 at 2.1 GFLOPs, 1.9x throughput (baseline 79.8 at 4.6; VTC-LFC 79.8 at 2.1, 1.1x), with channel pruning included
notes: [core] Joint token merging and channel pruning for DeiT with ImageNet results and transfer to ADE20K, COCO and other dense tasks; the DeiT-S numbers include both parts (ATME alone: 54.4% fewer FLOPs on DeiT-S in the ablation). Asymmetric token merging (ATME): before MHSA of selected layers the token grid is reshaped and two adjacent tokens (horizontal HTM, then vertical VTM at a later layer) are concatenated and fused by LayerNorm + a linear layer, halving the tokens while keeping a regular grid (operation cluster: fixed neighbour grouping with learned fusion, no scoring). Merging layers are chosen by hand to meet a FLOPs target (e.g. layers 5 and 8 for DeiT-S). Pretrained DeiTs are compressed in one fine-tuning run with hard distillation. Throughput is given only as a speed ratio (RTX 3090, batch 256), so deits_throughput is ?. No code link in the paper. Read the arXiv camera-ready version.
evidence: "we group and concatenate two adjacent tokens horizontally" (III-B, HTM); "we hierarchically alternatively utilize horizontal and vertical token merging before MHSA through the whole network for the token pruning" (III-B); "The proposed joint compression method can be seamlessly applied to prune well pretrained ViTs through a single finetuning process." (I. Introduction)

name: Vision-MoR
backbones: Vision-MoR Small; Base; Large; X-Large (own recursive ViTs)
main_result: Vision-MoR Small (ImageNet-1k): top-1 74.6 at 0.14 GFLOPs, 38.7K img/s on A100 (SHViT-S1 72.8; EfficientViT-M2 70.8)
notes: [core] Recursive ViT (shared middle blocks) with per-patch early exit from the recursion loop, trained from scratch and compared with lightweight backbones rather than with token reduction methods. A spatial router (two shifted-window attention rounds + MLP) gives depth logits per patch; at each recursion step a sigmoid gate keeps the top-k tokens and the others exit and are passed directly to the output head (operation halt). The kept fraction follows a target capacity (e.g. 0.5) with a warm-up during training, so the count per step is fixed by top-k; the paper also mentions hard routing by argmax over depths and does not say which is used at inference. Trained 300 epochs from scratch. GPU/CPU/ONNX throughput (A100) and batch-1 latency (3.63 ms, GH200). Also COCO detection. Not DeiT-sized, so the deits columns are empty. No code link in the paper.
evidence: "Based on the top-k gating values, selected tokens proceed to the next block" (Recursive Computation with Dynamic Token Allocation); "Others exit the computation loop and are passed directly to the output head." (same section); "All models are trained from scratch using the AdamW optimizer" (Experiment Setting)

name: MPM
backbones: ViT-T/16; ViT-S/16; ViT-B/16; ViT-B/8; ViT-L/16 (Segmenter); DeiT-B; EVA-01 (ViT-Adapter + Mask2Former)
main_result: Seg-S/16 (ADE20K): mIoU 45.1 at about 54 GFLOPs, 431 FPS (baseline 45.3 at 76.9 GFLOPs, 333 FPS; ToMe 45.5 at about 59, 388 FPS) on H100, batch 32
notes: [core] Training-free token merging for ViT semantic segmentation with end-to-end latency on H100 (with and without FlashAttention-2) and Raspberry Pi 5 (batch 1 and 2). Cosine similarity over all image tokens, each token's nearest neighbour, and only mutual nearest-neighbour pairs are averaged; tokens without a mutual partner stay as singletons. Inserted before blocks 2 and 5 (0-based); a stored merge map copies merged features back to the full grid before the decoder. There is no keep rate or threshold: the number of merges depends on the image (schedule other). No code link in the paper.
evidence: "MPM computes cosine affinities between tokens, forms pairs using a deterministic mutual nearest-neighbor rule, and merges each accepted pair by simple averaging." (1. Introduction); "MPM has no learned parameters and no continuous compression knob (no keep-rate or threshold)." (1. Introduction); "in practice, not all tokens find mutual partners, so the realized reduction is data-dependent" (3.2); "a saved merge map enables exact restoration of the original sequence length via a single gather operation before the decoder" (3)

name: Edge-RecViT
backbones: Edge-RecViT Tiny; Small; Base (12-layer ViT sizes with a shared middle block)
main_result: Edge-RecViT Small (ImageNet-1k): top-1 80.3 at 6.3 GFLOPs, 6.0M parameters (DeiT-S 79.8 at 9.2 GFLOPs in the paper's 1 MAC = 2 FLOPs convention)
notes: [core] Per-token adaptive depth in a recursive ViT (head layer, one shared hidden layer reused up to 10 times, tail layer) with ImageNet comparisons to DynamicViT, A-ViT, EViT, ATS and ToMe. An edge-aware ranker (2-layer MLP before the transformer) gives each token a depth 1-12 by argmax; a token stops at its depth and keeps its last state, the class token always runs all 12 layers (operation halt, per-token depth = halting). Losses keep the depth distribution stable and balanced. The ImageNet model is described as "full fine-tuning (no freezing) for 300 epochs" without naming a starting checkpoint, while CIFAR models are trained from scratch, so training is ?. The architecture differs from DeiT-S (shared weights) and FLOPs use 1 MAC = 2 FLOPs, so the deits columns are left ?. Only FLOPs and parameters, no latency.
evidence: "The EARR, placed prior to the transformer, evaluates each token’s semantic richness and determine its computation depth accordingly" (1. Introduction); "For each token i, computation terminates at its designated depth" (3.2); "For ImageNet-1K, we perform full fine-tuning (no freezing) for 300 epochs" (4.1)

name: SEPatch3D
backbones: ViT-L (StreamPETR, DETR3D, Sparse4Dv2); ViT-B (SAM-pretrained); ToC3D ViT-L
main_result: StreamPETR ViT-L (nuScenes val, 320x800): NDS 61.2 / mAP 52.1 at 250.2 ms (baseline 61.2 / 52.1 at 317.0 ms; ToC3D-fast 60.9 at 281.0 ms) on RTX 3090
notes: [application] Token compression for ViT backbones of sparse multi-view 3D object detectors (autonomous driving, nuScenes and Argoverse 2). Per frame, the patch size is switched between two preset sizes (e.g. 17/18 or 18/20 px) from the mean depth of the previous frame's object queries and its trend (schedule input-adaptive, per frame); FlexiViT-style flexible patch embedding gives the coarse tokens. Patches with above-mean entropy (after cross-attention with motion-aligned history queries) are selected, and these coarse tokens are enriched from the 16 px fine tokens by cross-attention; no token is dropped after embedding. Training (supplementary): 24 epochs of the detector with flexible patch embedding, then 12 epochs for the new modules, following StreamPETR. Latency of whole model and backbone on RTX 3090; batch size not stated.
evidence: "assigns small patches to scenes containing nearby objects to preserve fine details and large patches to background-dominated scenes to reduce computation cost" (Abstract); "patches whose entropy values exceed the mean entropy of all patches in the scene are selected" (3.3); "the first 24 epochs are used to train the detector with the flexible patch embedding module" (Supplementary, 1. More Implementation Details)

name: BiGain
main_result: Stable Diffusion 2.0 (ImageNet-1k, 70% merge ratio): diffusion-classifier accuracy +7.15 and FID 0.34 better than ToMe
notes: [generation] Training-free token compression for diffusion models that is judged both on generation (FID) and on diffusion-classifier accuracy (class-conditional denoising error). Two operators: (1) Laplacian-gated token merging: a Laplacian filter on the hidden-state grid scores local frequency, the lowest-scoring token in each stride becomes a destination, and source tokens merge into destinations by bipartite matching on similarity, with unmerge afterwards (as in ToMeSD); (2) Interpolate-Extrapolate KV downsampling: keys and values are pooled with a mix of nearest and average pooling while queries stay intact (operation other). A blockwise adaptive merging variant pools s x s blocks under a quantile threshold. Fixed merge ratio or downsampling factor. Only FLOPs, no wall-clock time.
evidence: "Laplacian-gated token merging, which encourages merges among spectrally smooth tokens while discouraging merges of high-contrast tokens, thereby retaining edges and textures" (Abstract); "present BiGain, a training-free, plug-and-play framework that preserves generation quality while markedly improving classification in accelerated diffusion models" (Abstract); "In each spatial stride, the lowest-scoring token is selected as a destination token, while the others form the source set." (Fig. 1)

name: HTTM
main_result: VGGT (NRGBD, stride 10): accuracy 0.012 / completeness 0.010 at 6.8 s with Q kept 20%, K/V 30% (VGGT* 0.010 / 0.010 at 13.9 s; FastVGGT 0.016 / 0.013 at 7.0 s); 1000 frames 102.8 s vs 724.6 s (7x) on A100
notes: [application] Training-free merging in the global attention layers of VGGT for multi-view 3D reconstruction. Queries and keys are merged separately in every attention head (values follow the keys) by ToMeSD-style src/dst matching on cosine similarity, attention runs on the shorter sequences, and the outputs are unmerged per head before concatenation. Tokens are reordered into spatio-temporal blocks (128 spatial tokens x 30 frames) and matching runs only inside a block; 10% outlier tokens with large deviation are excluded from merging under a global budget. Fixed ratios (90% of queries merged, 70% of keys/values). Latency on A100 in bfloat16 with FlashAttention. No code link in the paper.
evidence: "we propose head-wise temporal merging (HTTM), a training-free 3D token merging method for accelerating VGGT" (Abstract); "we merge the top-r src tokens with the highest similarity scores into their best-matching dst token" (3.1); "We merge 90% of the query tokens and filter 10% outliers" (4.1)

name: Co-Me
main_result: VGGT (DTU-MVS depth, 32 frames): L1 1.10 cm at 788 ms, 7.73x vs VGGT 6094 ms (memory-efficient VGGT* 1266 ms, L1 0.89; FastVGGT 2003 ms) on H100; up to 16.2x on RealEstate-10K with 128 frames
notes: [application] Token merging for visual geometric transformers (VGGT, Pi3, DA3, MapAnything) in depth, pose and point-map estimation. A light confidence predictor (MLP, single-head attention, Conv2D) is distilled from the frozen model's own confidence map with a ranking loss (TartanAir, under one H100 hour) and placed in the middle of the encoder. Tokens are split into fixed groups of 3x3; a group whose mean predicted confidence is below the p-th percentile over the sequence (p=0.5) is averaged into one token for the remaining blocks (attention and MLP, with an attention bias log n) and split back before the head. The fraction is fixed per sequence but can differ between images. The base model is never updated. Latencies on H100 (also Jetson Thor and RTX 5090); single-frame latency is given for NYUd-v2 and ETH3D. Project page co-me-tokens.github.io; no code repository named in the paper.
evidence: "distilled a light-weight confidence predictor to rank tokens by uncertainty and selectively merge low-confidence ones" (Abstract); "For each group, if the average confidence falls below the p-th percentile across all groups in the image sequence, it is marked for merging." (3.2); "Importantly, we never update or back-propagate through the visual geometric model" (3.1)

name: LiteVGGT
main_result: VGGT (ScanNet-50, 1000 images): Chamfer distance 0.428 at 127.2 s (VGGT* 0.485 at 1275.1 s; FastVGGT 0.436 at 258.3 s) on H20, with fine-tuning and FP8
notes: [application] Token merging around the global attention of VGGT for large-scale 3D reconstruction. A geometry-aware map (Sobel image gradient + local token variance) marks the top 10% tokens per frame as kept (GA tokens); dst tokens are all first-frame tokens and the lowest-scoring token of each 2x2 cell in other frames; all remaining src tokens merge into their most similar dst token (cosine) and are copied back after attention. Merge indices are computed once every 6 layers and reused. The final LiteVGGT also fine-tunes the aggregator and heads (20K iterations, 8 H20 GPUs) and uses FP8; the ablation also reports the merging without fine-tuning, hence mixed. Criterion other = image-gradient and variance map (not a model gradient). Project page only (garlicba.github.io/LiteVGGT), no code repository named in the paper.
evidence: "Src tokens are merged into the most similar dst tokens via cosine similarity-based feature averaging, with token replication (unmerging) restoring sequence length for dense prediction." (1. Introduction); "To eliminate redundant computation, we cache and reuse merge indices across adjacent layers." (1. Introduction); "Building on VGGT’s pretrained checkpoints, we fine-tune the aggregator and prediction heads" (3.5)

name: SRE-Merge
main_result: TransReID ViT-B/16 (Market-1501): Rank-1 95.8 / mAP 89.2 at 15.53 GFLOPs, 416.62 img/s (TransReID 95.6 / 89.3 at 20.41 GFLOPs, 335.73 img/s; ToMe 94.9 / 88.6) on A100
notes: [application] Training-free token merging for ViT-based person re-identification (Market-1501, MSMT17, Occluded-Duke) on a trained TransReID. Token importance (SE-Mass) is class-token attention per head weighted by the local attention entropy of each head and a centred Gaussian spatial prior; tokens are split into two sets by alternating positions in the SE-Mass order, matched by feature similarity combined with a mass-derived context term, and fused with mass weights and a norm-preserving rescale. r=8 tokens merged per layer in layers 1-10 (r=17 in a comparison). DeiT-S ImageNet top-1 79.41 (ToMe 79.39) is from Table 6, which gives no GFLOPs or throughput. Throughput batch size not stated. No code link in the paper.
evidence: "we propose SRE-Merge, a training-free framework designed for discriminative token compression" (1. Introduction); "Hybrid Context-Affinity Matching (HCA-Match), which guides precise pair selection by combining feature similarity with mass-derived context" (1. Introduction); "our token merging is applied to layers 1 to 10 of the model, with the number of merged tokens per layer set to r=8" (4.2)

backbones: Segmenter with DeiT-B; NViT-pruned DeiT-B (with ToMe, ALGM, CTS)
main_result: DeiT-B Segmenter (ADE20K, about 3.7x fewer FLOPs): ToMe 23.94 clean / 16.86 corrupted mIoU at 35.08 GFLOPs, NViT-S pruning 45.30 / 32.86 at 33.82, prune-then-merge 45.71 / 34.33 at 34.84 (baseline 47.22 / 35.58 at 129.70)
notes: [analysis] Comparison study, not a reduction method: token compression (ToMe, ALGM, CTS) versus structural pruning (NViT) for ViT semantic segmentation under matched FLOPs on ADE20K, Cityscapes and their corrupted versions. Finding: token compression keeps near-baseline mIoU at mild reduction (1.4-1.9x) but drops sharply at 3.4-3.8x (ToMe collapses on ADE20K; ALGM and CTS degrade more gracefully), while pruning degrades smoothly; moderate pruning followed by moderate ToMe (prune-then-merge) gives the best accuracy-robustness trade-off at high compression. All models are fine-tuned on the segmentation set with the ALGM-Segmenter recipe. Only GFLOPs, no latency.
evidence: "we benchmark representative token compression and structural pruning methods for ViT-based semantic segmentation under matched FLOPs" (Abstract); "token compression is highly effective at mild reductions but degrades sharply when compression becomes severe" (Abstract)

notes: [analysis] Survey, not a method: reviews dynamic neural networks in three groups (sample-wise, spatial-wise with pixel-, region- and resolution-level adaptation, temporal-wise for video and text). Written mainly about CNNs and RNNs; dynamic vision Transformers with early exiting or token sparsification appear only as a future direction (Sec. 7.2). Useful as background for input-adaptive computation, early exit and token skimming. Target set to other because the survey covers images, video and text.
evidence: "In this survey, we comprehensively review this rapidly developing area by dividing dynamic networks into three main categories" (Abstract); "recent work has proposed dynamic vision Transformers with adaptive early exiting [271] or token sparsification [272], [273]" (7.2)
